capitals.name: Kinshasa (Léopoldville until 1966)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Kinshasa (named Léopoldville until 1966)'. The coordinates are the city's modern position.

rulers.name: Mobutu Sese Seko
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Seized power in the coup of 24 November 1965, announced the renaming as Zaire on 27 October 1971 and 'fled into exile in Morocco on 17 May' 1997 (infobox 'Mobutu overthrown: 17 May 1997'; the page gives no regnal list).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Zaire row begins in 1973, but the Republic of Zaire was announced on 27 October 1971; for 1971-1972 the same outline is in the Democratic Republic of the Congo row (2,307,837 km2). No territorial change at the rename.

correction.text: the same state in its first Zaire years: the shape of the Democratic Republic of the Congo row alive in 1971, unchanged by the renaming of 27 October 1971

keyframe_review.note: 2,307,837 km2 for 1973-1991 against the infobox 2,345,409 km2 (no year given): ratio 0.98. The shape is the whole country; the Shaba invasions of 1977 and 1978 and the Kolwezi battle are carried by contest events, since the rebels held no ground for a year.
Same outline and area as 1973 (2,307,837 km2) for 1992-1995; the page's body text calls the years from 1990 the 'Third Congolese Republic', which does not change the territory.

New keyframe: Cliopatria draws 1996 onward under the Democratic Republic of the Congo row (2,307,837 km2), but the state was still Zaire until Mobutu fled on 17 May 1997. The AFDL rebellion held the east from 1996 (contest events); the shape is the whole country.

correction.text: the shape of the Democratic Republic of the Congo row alive in 1996, which is Zaire until the AFDL takes Kinshasa and the name is reverted on 21 May 1997

region.text: the whole country, renamed the Republic of Zaire

ledger.note: 27 October 1971: Mobutu renames the country the Republic of Zaire. 'He announced the renaming of the country as the Republic of Zaire on 27 October 1971'; the infobox gives 'the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1965 to 1971 and the Republic of Zaire from 1971 to 1997'. The same state under a new name, with the same land.

region.text: the south-west of Shaba: Dilolo, Kapanga, Kasaji and Mutshatsha, taken by the FNLC from 8 March 1977

ledger.note: 8 March 1977: Katangan rebels cross from Angola in the Shaba I invasion. 'The invaders launched a three-pronged attack on 8 March 1977, crossing the Angola-Zaire border on bicycles'; the US embassy confirmed Dilolo and Kapanga captured, and on 25 March 'the FAZ abandoned Mutshatsha, and the FNLC entered it', 130 km from the Kolwezi mining area. The page gives towns, not a boundary: the zone is two circles round Dilolo and Kasaji.

region.text: the south-west of Shaba, from which the FNLC was expelled by 26 May 1977

ledger.note: 26 May 1977: the Shaba I invasion ends in Zairian victory. Infobox: 'Date: 8 March - 26 May 1977', 'Result: Zairian victory, FNLC expelled from Shaba'; Moroccan troops had been airlifted to Kolwezi on 9 April and the allies recaptured Mutshatsha on 25 April.

region.text: the mining town where the battle was fought in May 1978

ledger.note: May 1978: the Shaba II invasion and the Battle of Kolwezi. 'In 1977 and 1978, Katangan rebels based in Angola launched two invasions, Shaba I and Shaba II'; 'The Battle of Kolwezi, fought in May 1978'. The page gives neither the day nor who held the town, so the zone is a 60 km circle round Kolwezi.

region.text: the mining town where the battle was fought in May 1978

ledger.note: May 1978: the Battle of Kolwezi is over within the month. The page dates the battle only to May 1978; Shaba I page: 'The Shaba II conflict began in May 1978'.

region.text: eastern Zaire, where the Hutu camps and the Banyamulenge were and where Kabila's AFDL rebelled in 1996

ledger.counterpart: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL)
ledger.note: 1996: the AFDL rebellion begins in eastern Zaire. 'In 1996, Laurent-Désiré Kabila, the head of the AFDL militia, led a popular rebellion against Mobutu'; Hutu militias used the refugee camps in eastern Zaire as bases and 'the Zairian government began to escalate its massacres in November 1996' against the Banyamulenge. The page gives no start month and no front line; the zone is the two Kivu provinces by the researcher's reading of 'eastern Zaire'.

region.text: the whole country, taken by the AFDL by the time it entered Kinshasa

ledger.counterpart: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL)
ledger.note: 17-21 May 1997: the AFDL takes the country and Mobutu falls. 'Mobutu fled into exile in Morocco on 17 May'; the AFDL 'marched unopposed into Kinshasa three days later'. The page gives no dates for Goma, Bukavu, Kisangani or Lubumbashi, so the zone is drawn as the whole country at the end.

region.text: the whole country, now under Kabila's Democratic Republic of the Congo

ledger.note: 21 May 1997: Zaire ends and the Democratic Republic of the Congo returns. 'On 21 May, Kabila officially reverted the name of the country to the Democratic Republic of the Congo'; the infobox 'Mobutu overthrown: 17 May 1997'. The land passes unchanged.

wars.name: Shaba I

zones.text: the south-west of Shaba: Dilolo, Kapanga, Kasaji, Mutshatsha

wars.outcome: Zairian victory, FNLC expelled from Shaba (infobox): Moroccan troops were airlifted to Kolwezi on French transport from 9 April, the allies recaptured Mutshatsha on 25 April and the war was over by 26 May 1977.

wars.name: Shaba II
wars.outcome: The pages opened give no result and no day: the Zaire page says only that 'the Battle of Kolwezi' was fought in May 1978 and that the invasion came from Angola.
wars.note: Shaba I page: 'The Shaba II conflict began in May 1978.' A gap-filler should open the Shaba II page.

wars.name: First Congo War
belligerents: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL)

zones.text: eastern Zaire, where the rebellion began in 1996

wars.outcome: AFDL victory: Mobutu fled into exile on 17 May 1997, the AFDL entered Kinshasa three days later and Kabila renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo on 21 May.
wars.note: The Zaire page does not name the First Congo War or date its cities; the democratic-republic-of-the-congo dossier cites the First Congo War page for 24 October 1996 to 16 May 1997.

certainty.note: Judgement, not read in the pages opened: the frontiers are the colonial-era treaty lines inherited at independence; the eastern frontier was not fought over by the pages' account. The rebel-held south-west of 1977 and east of 1996-1997 are contests, not borders.

notes: SAME STATE AS democratic-republic-of-the-congo: Cliopatria has 'Democratic Republic of the Congo' 1960-1972 and 1996-2024 and 'Zaire' 1973-1995 (Wikidata Q6500954); the Zaire page's infobox says 'officially the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1965 to 1971 and the Republic of Zaire from 1971 to 1997', a rename, not a new state. The democratic-republic-of-the-congo dossier (another group, 1960-2024) already carries 1971-1997 as a rename pair and a keyframe that points at the Zaire shape. This dossier is written because the brief assigns the 'zaire' slug; the integrator should keep ONE of the two and, if it keeps the Congo dossier, fold in this one's ledger (Shaba I 1977, Shaba II 1978) and drop the zaire slug, so that the state keeps a single colour (master plan rule 2). Two pages only (budget 1-2): Zaire and Shaba I. NOT SETTLED: (1) Shaba II: the Zaire page gives only 'the Battle of Kolwezi, fought in May 1978'; who held Kolwezi, the day and the rebels' ground are not on the pages opened (a gap-filler should open the Shaba II page); (2) the First Congo War: the Zaire page gives 1996, November 1996 massacres, 17 May 1997 and 21 May 1997, and no city dates; the other dossier's First Congo War page gives 24 October 1996 as the start and the dates of Lubumbashi and Kinshasa, so the start year agrees and the month here is left empty; the contest zone is the two Kivu provinces at the start and the whole country at the end; (3) Rwandan refugee camps in eastern Zaire from 1994 are only 'by 1996' on this page; the Banyamulenge are mentioned without a date; (4) Cabinda: the page does not mention it, and the neighbour estado-novo row (1979-1995, a 6,900 km2 patch at Cabinda) is Angola's enclave, not Zairean land; (5) Zaire's end year 1997 differs from Cliopatria's Zaire row (to 1995) because the row hands over to the Democratic Republic of the Congo row from 1996 although Mobutu fell in May 1997: two new keyframes (1971-1972 and 1996-1997) point at the other row's shape. Gazetteer: all names resolve (Dilolo, Kasaji, Kolwezi as places; Nord-Kivu and Sud-Kivu as admin1); Kapanga, Mutshatsha, Sandoa and Kisenge are not in the gazetteer and are only named in text.
